System

Character persistence, schema, command receipts and sessions

Durability means accepted inventory, currency, quests and progression survive process loss. A UE zone keeps a short-lived authoritative session cache, while one authenticated backend commits durable relational records and audit receipts.

Scope and player interaction

Durability means accepted inventory, currency, quests and progression survive process loss. A UE zone keeps a short-lived authoritative session cache, while one authenticated backend commits durable relational records and audit receipts.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase05committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Loading → Ready → CommandPending → ReconciliationRequired → ReadOnlyDegraded → LeaseLost → InvalidRecord

WBP_Diagnostics observes results from URPGCharacterServiceAdapter. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_ServicePolicy_Development. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
CharacterId UUID; AccountId UUID; SchemaVersion integer; ContentVersion integer
CharacterRevision bigint >=0; SessionEpoch bigint >=1; OwnerZoneInstanceId UUID
CommandId UUID scoped to authenticated subject and operation; RequestHash immutable
Receipt: Pending|Committed|Rejected with immutable result and resulting revision
Quantities and BaseCurrency: bounded integers with database checks
OwnedItemId UUID for nonstackables; ItemDefinitionId stable string; no pointer serialization
LeaseExpiryUtc and LastDurableSafeLocation: backend-controlled values

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGCharacterServiceAdapterImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_DiagnosticsLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
LoadCharacter(CharacterId, SessionProof) -> VersionedSnapshot|Forbidden|InvalidRecord
SubmitCharacterCommand(CommandEnvelope) -> Committed|Rejected|Unknown; asynchronous server adapter
GetCommandReceipt(CommandId) -> Receipt|NotFound; safe retry reconciliation
RenewSessionLease(CharacterId, Epoch) -> Renewed|Fenced; server/backend
ReleaseSessionLease(CharacterId, Epoch) -> Released|AlreadyReleased

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Zone adapter authenticates as a trusted server and includes CharacterId, zone ID, fencing epoch, expected revision, command ID and bounded validated payload.
  2. Backend validates the server capability and current lease; it never trusts a client to select a privileged operation or pass a completed gameplay event.
  3. Open a short database transaction; look up or insert the unique command record and compare request hash. A reused ID with different data rejects.
  4. Lock all affected ownership/economy/source rows in a consistent order, revalidate constraints, apply all changes, increment revision and store result/audit/outbox rows atomically.
  5. Commit before returning success. Zone applies the returned snapshot/delta on the game thread only if its session epoch and request generation still match.
  6. Timeout means outcome unknown: suspend conflicting writes, query receipt or retry the identical command. A committed result is returned without consuming/granting again.
  7. On restart, revoke expired leases, migrate supported records, and restore accepted facts; no widget or local SaveGame can override the snapshot.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Create the small backend as one service with routes grouped by domain, one relational database and migrations. Compare .NET 10 ASP.NET Core with TypeScript/Node; this guide chooses .NET 10 for typed contracts and a long support window, not because Node is invalid.
  2. Define the database schema in sources/database-models.json and implement migrations in a separate backend repository; this documentation contains no production service implementation. Use a local isolated database and nonproduction accounts.
  3. Add HTTP/JSON adapter dependencies to the native RPG module as needed after installed engine API review. Use asynchronous requests; never block the game thread on SQL or HTTP.
  4. URPGCharacterServiceAdapter belongs to the server process lifecycle; client account adapter has separate capabilities. Keep endpoint allowlists and secrets in environment/deployment configuration, not Data Assets distributed to clients.
  5. Create ServiceFixture_CharacterStore with committed, rejected, delayed-after-commit, stale-epoch and corrupted-record scenarios. Reopen ARPGZoneGameMode to require successful hydration before possession.
  6. Expose immutable snapshot getters/delegates to Blueprint, not arbitrary SQL or SetCurrency functions. Test adapter callbacks after actor teardown and server travel.

Reopen Phase05 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: ServiceFixture_CharacterStore / Account_A / Character_A / L_NetworkLab. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Lost response after commit -> GetCommandReceipt returns one original result; no second grant.
Same command ID/different payload -> IdempotencyConflict; original receipt remains unchanged.
Old source server uses epoch N after transfer to N+1 -> SessionFenced; no write.
Concurrent withdraw/craft using same item -> consistent lock/revision policy accepts only a valid serial outcome.
Unknown schema/content ID -> InvalidRecord or UnsupportedContentVersion; quarantine and show safe login error, not silently delete items.
Database serialization/deadlock retry -> retry the entire transaction under bounded policy, never only the final reward insert.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Proposed command payload limit 32 KiB, bounded retry with jitter, 30-second session lease renewed every 10 seconds. Tune under actual load and failure tests; no unbounded in-memory reward queue.

Ledger fields include command/character/zone/epoch/revision/reason/definition IDs and deltas. Exclude secrets, raw provider proofs and unnecessary chat content. Backups require restore drills, not merely successful backup jobs.
